_comment: Delta-neutral BTC strangle on Delta Exchange India. 'Delta neutral' here means PREMIUM SYMMETRY, not option greeks: the two legs are re-balanced whenever one leg's premium reaches 2x the other's. Ported from live_trading_options/delta_neutral (NIFTY+SENSEX). PAPER ONLY in v1 — there is no live order path yet.
_contract_value_note: BTC per contract, from Delta's own product master. A premium of $150 therefore costs 150 * 0.001 = $0.15 per contract. Read from the exchange at engine start; this value is only the fallback.
_settlement_note: Every daily BTC option settles at 17:30 IST (12:00 UTC) and the next day's chain lists at the same moment. Every session profile below is defined against that single fixed point.
_usd_inr_note: Display only — every number the strategy decides on is USD, because that is what Delta quotes, margins and settles in. This rate is used solely to print a rupee figure beside the dollar one so the results read against the NSE books. Refresh it before quoting results.

ist_day.label: A - IST day session (0 DTE, awake hours)
ist_day._note: Sells the contract expiring TODAY at 17:30, entering with ~7.7h of life left. Closest analogue to the NSE 0-DTE book and the only profile you are awake for end to end.

full_cycle.label: B - full expiry cycle (one strangle per expiry)
full_cycle._note: Enters 5 minutes after the new chain lists and holds the whole ~23.6h cycle through US and Asian hours. Higher target premium than A because the contract has ~24h of life at entry rather than ~8h.

continuous.label: C - continuous (always short, rolls every expiry)
continuous._note: Same clock as B, opposite temperament. Neither a double stop-out nor the max-loss ends the cycle — it re-enters at the next adjustment window, subject to max_fresh_entries. B measures one strangle per expiry; C measures always being short.

_calibration_note: Target 50 premium on ALL THREE profiles, set 2026-09-13 after four days of live paper said the previous calibration was wrong. That calibration matched NIFTY's moneyness (delta ~0.14, giving A=70 and B/C=150) on the reasoning that equal delta is equal risk. It is not: BTC moves far more relative to its option premium than NIFTY does, and the attribution showed EVERY stop-out landed on a leg sold near that target while the cheaper far-OTM legs never stopped and made money. A single flat target across profiles also makes the session comparison cleaner, since target no longer varies with the profile.
_sizing_note: All three profiles trade the SAME 1000 contracts at the SAME 50 target, so session length is the only variable between them. 1000 contracts = 1.0 BTC per leg, about $79k notional per leg at BTC 79k. At target both legs pay 50, so the credit is 50 * 0.001 * 1000 * 2 = $100 per fresh strangle.
_size_change_note: Raised 100 -> 1000 on 2026-09-09, and the depth was CHECKED before doing it rather than assumed: the top bid held ~10,000 contracts on every strike then in play (81000CE, 76400PE, 80000CE), so 1000 fills entirely at level 1 with zero slippage. That matters because the paper fill model takes the whole order at the touch and does NOT walk the book — at a size the top level cannot absorb, paper would quietly report fills nobody could get. Re-check depth before raising again, and be aware it is thinner on far-OTM strikes than on the ones sampled. Changing this mid-cycle is safe: the controller refuses to adopt a saved position whose legs are the old size, closing and recording that cycle instead of running a strangle with mismatched legs.
_shared_note: Everything below applies to all three profiles. Only the session shape and its target/stop are allowed to differ, so that a difference in the month's results can be attributed to the session and not to the parameters.
_sl_note: The stop is NOT a fixed level. Every leg's stop sits at this multiple of the pair's CURRENT COMBINED premium (CE mark + PE mark), recomputed at entry and at every 15-minute window. Sell two legs at 50 and the stop is 1.2 x 100 = 120, a doubling — reasonable. Six hours later the same pair is worth 8 + 9 and the stop is 1.2 x 17 = 20.4, still proportional; a FIXED 100 there could never protect anything and the leg would run unbounded to the square-off. It cannot fire on placement either: 1.2 x (a+b) always exceeds a and b individually. Recomputed only while BOTH legs are alive — single-legged, 'combined' would mean one leg's own premium and the stop would clamp 20% above the market at the worst possible moment.
_ratio_note: Adjust when max(leg premium) >= ratio * min(leg premium). The SMALLER leg is the one replaced.
_windows_note: Adjustments are evaluated ONLY inside a 60-second window every 15 minutes, starting 15 minutes after entry and stopping 10 minutes before square-off. Outside a window nothing is ever adjusted — that rule is what stops the strategy reacting to every wiggle.
_max_loss_note: USD MAGNITUDE. Own-book MTM <= -max_loss ends the cycle (A and B) or pauses it (C). MUST sit ABOVE the worst case the leg stops themselves allow, or it fires first and the per-leg stops never get to work — the trap that cost the NSE book a day. At 1000 contracts and the 1.2x combined stop, the worst an ORDERLY pair of stop-outs can cost is bounded by the stop in force at the time; at entry that is 1.2*100 = 120 per leg against a 50 entry, so (120-50)*0.001*1000*2 = $140. $450 and $900 sit well clear. THESE SCALE WITH `contracts` — raising size without raising these would make the loss limit fire before the leg stops could work, and the engine refuses to run a profile in that state. The engine recomputes this at start and REFUSES TO RUN a profile whose limit sits below its own worst case, rather than leaving it to be discovered on a bad day.

fees._note: Delta charges the LOWER of 0.01% of notional (spot * contract_value * size) and 3.5% of premium, per side. Modelled on every simulated fill because a month of paper without costs would flatter a strategy that adjusts this often — A/B/C differ in how many times they trade, so fees are exactly the kind of thing that could reverse the ranking.

slippage._note: A paper SELL fills at the best BID and a paper BUY at the best ASK — never at the mark. Filling at the mark would hand the paper book half the spread on every leg, and this strategy trades often enough for that to be the whole result. Where a side of the book is missing, the mark is used and the fill is flagged.

_chain_span_note: Strikes each side of ATM to track. Wider than the NSE book's 15 because BTC's daily grid tightens to 100 near the money, so 20 strikes is a narrower band in percentage terms than it sounds.
_stall_note: No usable chain refresh for this long during a session and the engine exits for a clean restart. Longer than the NSE engine's 90s because this one polls REST on a cadence rather than consuming a push socket.
_poll_note: Chain refresh cadence. 3 rate-limit units per call against a 20,000/5min budget, so 5s uses ~3.6% of quota. Decisions are never faster than a 60-second window, so this is already far finer than the strategy needs.

live_orders._comment: PAPER ONLY. There is no live order path in v1 — no API key is even required to run this. When live is built it goes through a signed REST client with its own client_order_id prefix as the own-book scope, rehearsed on testnet (cdn-ind.testnet.deltaex.org) first.
